source_observation: resolve_access looks up denied_commands by command, maps the vector to any(origin.matches(context)), then calls is_some() on the Option. Therefore the code path returns the deny branch whenever any deny entry exists for the command, regardless of the boolean produced by the origin predicate.
Denied ResolvedCommand values retain capability window and webview selectors, but resolve_access does not test those selectors before taking the deny branch.
contract_evidence: Capability documentation describes capabilities as access boundaries for matching windows/webviews and optional remote URL contexts.
Resolved::resolve copies capability context, window patterns, and webview patterns into both allowed_commands and denied_commands.
The allow branch of resolve_access requires both origin and window/webview selector matches.
prepared_controls: allow local/main plus deny remote/main: local/main should remain allowed
allow local/main plus deny local/admin: local/main should remain allowed
allow local/main plus deny local/main: matching deny should still override the allow
repair_sketch: If the prepared controls reproduce the suspected over-denial, replace the current map(...).is_some() deny check with is_some_and(...), requiring origin.matches(&cmd.context) and either a matching webview or window pattern, mirroring the allow selector semantics.
